summary: Machine-level gain: none (parity). The shipped state d5f5aa80fb92d7a5 is an amdclang build of a rewritten source plus a launch change, so its 1.68x over the shipped baseline (240 pairs, CI 1.679-1.688; 0.1116 ms vs 0.1880 ms) is credited to amdclang, not to machine-IR work. The rewrite handles two rotation pairs (16 bytes) per thread: x is read once with one global_load_dwordx4 instead of twice with dword loads (the baseline re-read x[gid+-1], so this was the 're-reads a tensor' case, reference headroom 1.79), cos/sin are dwordx4, the store is dwordx4, with a slow path for tails and the rotary wrap; block 64 instead of 256 adds 1.026x. The result sits at headroom 1.06 of the memory floor; on top of it, the hand-written machine IR (x load issued before the modulo, args loaded once, compact slow path) measured 1.0009 (CI 0.9993-1.0025, 240 pairs) and coarsen lost, so the kernel is at the memory floor and no machine-level win exists over the new amdclang build.

friction: No scalar integer division: a wave-uniform modulo (freq index of lane 0, then +lane) cannot be hoisted to SGPRs, so the per-lane reciprocal modulo stays; here it is hidden behind the load anyway.

compare() results are not recorded as a bench verdict on the state: states ranked only through compare (coarsen, block 1024, hand IR) show bench=null in list_states, so a later session cannot see they were measured unless it reads the report.

The split between 'source credit' and 'machine credit' is ambiguous for relaunch: block 64 was made with relaunch on a source state (a machine-level tool) but is a launch knob amdclang's build could have; I reported it as amdclang's.
Could not tell from the tools whether a masked-off (exec=0 lanes) global_load still counts in vmcnt; I used full vmcnt(0) waits in the slow path to be safe.
lessons: mo_rope_fwd (elementwise pair rotation, 4 B per lane, x read twice per element as x[gid] and x[gid+-1]): two pairs per thread with one dwordx4 load of x, dwordx4 cos/sin and a dwordx4 store gave 1.64x at the source level (0.187 -> 0.114 ms), taking headroom from 1.79 to 1.09. A neighbour read (x[gid+-1]) is a re-read: group the neighbours into one lane.

On that 16-B-per-lane loop-free state: block 64 is 1.026x over block 256 (240-pair-class CI 1.021-1.032), block 1024 is 0.915x, coarsen 2 is 0.952x, coarsen 4 is 0.883x. Confirms: many short one-wave workgroups each touching 1 KB contiguous are best; coarsen only pays on 4-B-per-lane kernels.

At headroom 1.06, issuing the main dwordx4 load ~25 VALU instructions earlier (before a reciprocal modulo) is exact parity (1.0009, CI +-0.16%): load latency overlap inside a straight-line wave does not matter once the kernel streams at ~4.8 TB/s.

amdclang compiles ext_vector_type(4)/aligned(4) float loads into global_load_dwordx4 and the pair rotation into v_pk_mul/v_pk_fma with op_sel swaps; no scratch, 22 VGPRs. A 32-bit unsigned modulo guarded by 'if (p >= k)' becomes an exec-masked reciprocal sequence (~25 instructions) and is not a bottleneck.

session.final:
No machine-level win on `mo_rope_fwd`: the kernel ends at the memory floor, and the only gain is a source rewrite that is credited to amdclang.

- **Shipped state:** `d5f5aa80fb92d7a5`, 1.68x over the baseline (0.1116 ms against 0.1880 ms, 240 pairs, CI 1.679–1.688), full battery passed.
- **What it does:** each thread handles two rotation pairs (16 bytes), so `x` is read once with a wide load instead of twice per element. This was the "re-reads a tensor" case: baseline headroom 1.79, now 1.06.
- **Launch:** block 64 instead of 256 adds 1.026x on top of the rewrite; block 1024 was 0.915x.
- **Machine IR on top:** a hand-written body that issues the `x` load before the modulo measured 1.0009 (CI 0.9993–1.0025, 240 pairs), which is parity.
- **Coarsen:** factor 2 was 0.952x and factor 4 was 0.883x against the rewritten source.

I stopped after those three different kinds of idea brought nothing over the block-64 state. The report is recorded with the tried list, friction and lessons.
